name: Syntax Highlighters
description: Libraries and tools that turn source code into highlighted output across every host language — regex-lexer engines, TextMate/Sublime-grammar engines, parse-tree-based engines, and highlight-first CLIs — compared across engine model, grammar and theme ecosystems, intermediate representations (token streams, scope stacks, styled spans, highlight events, hast), output formats beyond HTML, runtime footprint, performance, and maintenance

groups.name: General Information
groups.description: Host language, form factor, licensing, and basic identifying information

attributes.name: Host Language
attributes.description: Language the engine is implemented in / primarily consumed from; multiple only when genuinely first-class in several

attributes.name: Form Factor
attributes.description: A library that ships its own CLI gets both Library and CLI

attributes.name: License
attributes.description: From LICENSE / package manifest; bundled grammars may carry different licences (see comment)

attributes.name: Repository
attributes.description: Canonical source repository

attributes.name: Package
attributes.description: Registry page (PyPI, crates.io, pkg.go.dev, RubyGems, npm, Packagist, NuGet, Hackage, Hex); for CLIs the official download page

attributes.name: Documentation
attributes.description: Dedicated docs site if present, else docs.rs / readthedocs / README

attributes.name: First Release
attributes.description: Year of first public release; informational rather than a ranking signal

attributes.name: Latest Version
attributes.description: Current stable version string; date checked noted in comment

groups.name: Highlighting Engine
groups.description: How the engine recognises syntax and what that means for accuracy, nesting, and incremental use

attributes.name: Engine Model
attributes.description: What actually executes at highlight time; a second tag only if the tool genuinely offers two engines

attributes.name: Regex Engine
attributes.description: Regex implementation that runs the grammars; n/a for parse-tree engines

attributes.name: Embedded Languages
attributes.description: Highlights nested languages (CSS/JS in HTML, fenced code in Markdown, injections) out of the box, at least HTML+JS+CSS

attributes.name: Language Auto-Detection
attributes.description: Can guess the language from content, not just filename/extension

attributes.name: Filename / Extension Mapping
attributes.description: Built-in filename/extension/shebang/mime → language lookup

attributes.name: Resumable Line State
attributes.description: Exposes per-line parse state that can be saved and resumed for line-by-line or viewport highlighting

attributes.name: Incremental Reparsing
attributes.description: Updates highlighting after an edit by reusing the previous parse (tree-sitter, Lezer)

attributes.name: Semantic Distinctions
attributes.description: Distinguishes roles beyond lexical class (definition vs call, parameter vs local) via a syntax tree or locals queries

groups.name: Language & Grammar Support
groups.description: Bundled languages, grammar formats, and which external grammar ecosystems can be reused

attributes.name: Bundled Languages
attributes.description: Distinct languages in the default/full distribution (aliases not counted); core vs full noted in comment

attributes.name: Grammar Format
attributes.description: Native grammar definition format; Code = lexers written in the host language

attributes.name: Grammar Ecosystem Compatibility
attributes.description: External grammar ecosystems it can consume directly; build-time conversion counts (noted in comment)

attributes.name: Runtime Grammar Loading
attributes.description: User can register a new or modified grammar at runtime without forking/rebuilding

attributes.name: Lazy Grammar Loading
attributes.description: Grammars load on demand rather than all bundled up front

attributes.name: Grammar Accuracy
attributes.description: 5 = tracks mainstream upstream grammars incl. modern syntax; 3 = solid for common constructs with known gaps; 1 = keyword/string/comment only

groups.name: Themes & Styling
groups.description: Bundled themes, theme formats, token naming, and class-based or multi-theme output

attributes.name: Bundled Themes
attributes.description: Themes/styles shipped by default; version noted in comment

attributes.name: Theme Format
attributes.description: Theme definition format(s) accepted; Code = themes defined in host-language code

attributes.name: Token Classification
attributes.description: How tokens are named for styling: hierarchical scopes, closed token set, tree-sitter captures, or Lezer tags

attributes.name: CSS Class Output
attributes.description: Can emit class names instead of inline styles

attributes.name: Multi-Theme Output
attributes.description: One render serves several themes (light/dark) via CSS variables or multiple class sets

groups.name: Intermediate Representations
groups.description: What an application can get besides a finished string: token streams, scope stacks, styled spans, events, hast, JSON

attributes.name: Public Token API
attributes.description: Documented public API yielding tokens/spans without rendering to a final format

attributes.name: IR Kinds
attributes.description: Kinds of documented intermediate representation exposed

attributes.name: Serializable IR
attributes.description: IR is plain data with documented serialization (JSON, hast, serde) suitable for caching or sending over the wire

attributes.name: Theme-Resolved Tokens
attributes.description: Can emit tokens with colours/styles already resolved from a theme, for non-CSS renderers

attributes.name: Source Offsets in IR
attributes.description: Tokens/events carry byte/char offsets or line/column back into the source

attributes.name: Custom Formatter API
attributes.description: Documented extension point for writing your own output formatter/renderer

attributes.name: Line Transforms / Decorations
attributes.description: Built-in mechanism to annotate lines/ranges (highlighted lines, diff markers, focus) on the IR before output

groups.name: Output Formats
groups.description: First-party output targets beyond HTML: terminal, print, image

attributes.name: Output Formats
attributes.description: First-party output targets only; community plugins noted in comment

attributes.name: Line Numbers
attributes.description: Built-in line-number output for at least one format

attributes.name: Streaming Output
attributes.description: Emits output incrementally (line-by-line or chunked) before the full input is consumed

attributes.name: Terminal-Ready
attributes.description: Ships an ANSI/terminal output path usable in CLIs without extra glue

groups.name: Runtime & Integration
groups.description: Native dependencies, browser/WASM support, sync vs async API, bindings, and package size

attributes.name: Native Dependencies
attributes.description: Native code linked or embedded; library named in comment

attributes.name: Runs in Browser
attributes.description: Usable client-side in a browser without a server

attributes.name: WASM Build
attributes.description: Officially compiles to or ships as WASM

attributes.name: Synchronous API
attributes.description: Can highlight synchronously after setup; async-only initialisation noted in comment

attributes.name: Bindings / Ports
attributes.description: Official or well-known bindings in other languages; project named in comment

attributes.name: Core Package Size
attributes.description: Minimal usable distribution: min+gzip core for JS, installed size otherwise; what was measured noted in comment

groups.name: Performance
groups.description: Throughput and initialisation cost, based on comparative benchmarks

attributes.name: Throughput Tier
attributes.description: Relative to fastest in a shared benchmark: top-tier ≤1.5×, fast 1.5–3×, moderate 3–10×, slow >10×

attributes.name: Initialization Cost
attributes.description: Time to first highlight: light <10 ms, moderate 10–100 ms, heavy >100 ms

groups.name: Ecosystem & Maintenance
groups.description: Popularity, release activity, documentation, notable users, and bus factor

attributes.name: GitHub Stars
attributes.description: Snapshot; date noted in comment

attributes.name: Monthly Downloads
attributes.description: From the primary registry; cross-registry numbers only roughly comparable — registry and date in comment

attributes.name: Last Release
attributes.description: Most recent stable release

attributes.name: Maintenance Status
attributes.description: Active = release/substantive commit in last 6 months; dormant = nothing in 24+ months, not archived

attributes.name: Documentation Quality
attributes.description: 5 = docs site with guides, API reference, language/theme catalog, migration notes; 3 = solid README + API reference; 1 = minimal or stale

attributes.name: Notable Users
attributes.description: 2–4 well-known projects or products using it

attributes.name: Bus Factor
attributes.description: Who maintains it
